Name: Mocktail Root Handler Routes
Description: Defines the routing configuration for the Mocktail root handler. this handler supports the following types of routes: 1)redirect: A route that automatically forwards requests to one or more target paths or an external URL. 2)dynamic: A route that is handled by a function defined in the root handler script, allowing for custom processing of requests. 3)static: A route that serves static files from a specified directory (in this case .files). 4)sub-handler: A route that delegates request handling to a separate handler script, allowing for modular and organized handling of specific paths or functionalities. 5)json-response: A route that responds with a predefined JSON object, useful for simple API endpoints or testing purposes.

Routes.Title: Redirect to User Handler
Routes.Description: The /usr* route handler, delegates handling of any requests to paths starting with /usr to the user-handler script located at ./res/handlers/usr/user-handler. This allows for modular handling of user-related routes and functionalities, keeping the root handler organized and focused on routing while the user-handler script can manage specific logic related to user operations.

Routes.Title: Redirect to System Handler
Routes.Description: The /sys* route handler, delegates handling of any requests to paths starting with /sys to the system-handler script located at ./res/handlers/sys/system-handler. This allows for modular handling of system-related routes and functionalities, keeping the root handler organized and focused on routing while the system-handler script can manage specific logic related to system operations.

Routes.Title: General System UI Resources, Static Wildcard Route
Routes.Description: The wildcard path for serving assets such as CSS, JS, images etc for the system handler's UIs. This route will attempt to match any request starting with /assets/ and serve the corresponding static file from the .files/ui directory. This allows for easy referencing of static resources in the HTML files served by the system handler, ensuring that the necessary assets are available for the UI to function properly.Note: Where a wildcard Path is used (i.e /assets/*)  the FilePath MUST refer to the base internal directory that the files should be served from such that [BASE_DIR]/[Relative_Request_Path_Reveived_To_Handler] resolves to the file on disk, failure to set this path correctly will result in 404 Not Found errors being returned to the client.
